newsitem.title: GERMANY: Top German economist urges reform for investment.
newsitem.headline: Top German economist urges reform for investment.

text.p: Germany must cut wage costs, step up innovation and increase competition between individual states to boost investment and improve its standing as a financial centre, a leading economist said on Wednesday.
"We have a pronounced weakness in investment," Horst Siebert, a member of the Bonn government's "five wise men" economic advisory council, told the daily Die Welt newspaper.

Siebert, who is also the president of the IfW economic institute in Kiel, said lack of investment in Germany was caused by unfavourable tax legislation and high labour costs, adding that one solution would be to induce more intensive competition between German states, or Laender.
While German companies had already made great efforts to reduce costs, jobs had nevertheless been lost, Siebert told the newspaper.
He said greater productivity and more innovation in the creation of new products was needed increase competitiveness and make it sustainable.

Looking at foreign exchange markets, Siebert said the recent decline of the mark versus the dollar, which he saw as a reaction to the impending single European currency, had helped German firms increase international competitiveness.
He said the mark, which was trading at 175.92 to the dollar in early business on Wednesday, was now relatively fairly valued.
